To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The auditory system is capable of detecting regularities in the acoustic input and 2) The auditory system uses these regularities to predict the upcoming acoustic signal and to select the most likely interpretation.

the auditory system continuously searches and extracts regularities from the incoming sound, and that the resulting representations serve as auditory percept objects, and that they are used for parsing the composite auditory input into coherent sequences.

the auditory cortex contains cells that are tuned to the regularities of the auditory input, that the auditory system is capable of generating predictions about the future sounds, that the predictions are based on the regularities of sound patterns, and that the predictions are used in the perceptual process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: (1) What is the neural basis for auditory perception?
how the brain constructs a representation of the external world, and how this representation is used for guiding behavior.
how regularities in sensory information are detected, represented, and utilized in perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the auditory system is a predictive processing system that uses regularities to construct a representation of the auditory world.
the auditory system continuously generates a model of the acoustic scene by detecting regularities in the input and using them to predict the incoming sounds.
the auditory system continuously extracts the regularities of the incoming sound, and that the extracted regularities are the perceptual objects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
auditory perceptual objects are the result of a predictive process that continuously extracts and updates representations of regularities from the acoustic signal.
the auditory system is not a passive detector, but an active generator of hypotheses about the world, based on the regularities it extracts from the input.

we are trying to understand how the auditory system extracts and represents the regularities in the acoustic input, and how the representations of regularities are used to generate predictions of the incoming sounds and to parse the composite auditory input into coherent sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the auditory system is equipped with a mechanism that allows it to construct and maintain representations of regularities in the acoustic signal.
auditory perception is not a passive process of detecting the physical properties of the incoming sounds.
the auditory scene analysis problem can be viewed as an inverse problem.
